newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UK steel firms complain to EU about Clabecq rescue.
newsitem.headline: UK steel firms complain to EU about Clabecq rescue.

text.p: British steelmakers have complained to the European Commission about a plan to salvage Belgian steel maker Forges de Clabecq, a Commission spokesman said on Saturday.

The spokesman said he had no details. But Belgian daily newspaper Le Soir said on Saturday that the British firms were particularly worried Clabecq would not reimburse Belgian subsidies declared illegal by the Commission in 1996.
The Belgian Walloon region and Italian-Swiss firm Duferco reached an agreement earlier this month for a partial takeover of bankrupt Clabecq.

Clabecq filed for bankruptcy after the Commission banned the Walloon region from injecting 1.5 billion Belgian francs ($42 million) into the loss-making firm and ordered that subsidies already granted, mainly in the form of bridging loans, be paid back.
Le Soir quoted Ian Rodgers, director of policy at the UK Steel Association, as saying Clabecq's new owners ought to be responsible for the reimbursement of the illegal aid.

The British association also argued that current work financed by the Walloon region on a channel between Bruxelles and Charleroi and at the Clabecq port and site also amounted to unauthorised subsidies to the Belgian steelworks, Le Soir said.

Finally, the Commission was also looking into a plan by the Walloon region to spend up to 900 million Belgian francs ($25 million) to help some 500 Clabecq workers expected to loose their jobs, it said. $1 = 35.6 francs
